note_on_method: Two different kinds of claim appear below and they are deliberately kept apart. Claims about the world — how many courts a park has, when it closes — come from Seattle Parks and Recreation and are cited. Claims about our own inventory — how many rows we hold, how many are unverified — are facts about this dataset, not about King County, and are worded so a reader cannot mistake one for the other. 'We hold 151 imported records for King County' is true and checkable; 'King County has 151 pickleball venues' would be neither.

slots.coverage: Three cities in King County are published here. Seattle came first, with twenty-four venues verified against Seattle Parks and Recreation's own records; Bellevue followed on 4 September 2026 with thirteen venues and forty-two courts read from the City of Bellevue's pages; and Kirkland joined the same day with three venues and ten courts. Together that is forty venues and a hundred and forty-four courts, and the county is still far larger than that. We hold a hundred and fifty-one imported records spanning twenty-eight King County cities, and outside those three, not one row has been checked against a named source, so not one of them appears on this site. Several more of those cities already hold three or more records, which means they clear the venue threshold on volume alone and are waiting on provenance rather than on discovery - Redmond with twelve records, Kent with nine, Auburn with seven, Issaquah and Mercer Island with six.
slots.distribution: The three published cities are a study in contrast, and the first contrast is about roofs. Every one of Seattle's ninety-two verified courts is outdoor; fourteen of Bellevue's forty-two are indoor, in three community centres and a fieldhouse. So on a wet January evening the verified pickleball in King County is almost entirely on the east side of Lake Washington, which is not a claim about where the courts are but about where the ones we can vouch for are covered. Within Seattle the courts cluster north and south - Green Lake Park East, Bitter Lake Playfield and Rainier Beach Playfield hold eight each - while Bellevue's largest single count is the six indoor courts at South Bellevue Community Center, and its outdoor provision runs to four courts each at Crossroads, Eastgate and Lakemont. Kirkland is a third case again, and it sits outside that comparison entirely: its ten courts are neither indoor nor outdoor here, because the City states which kind of court each one is - "6 pickleball courts", not six tennis courts striped for it - and never says whether they have a roof. All ten close at dusk, which answers the question in practice without answering it in the data.
slots.gaps: This page said, a day before Bellevue was published, that it was "a Seattle page wearing a county heading" and that Bellevue, Redmond, Kent and Renton would each need their parks pages read individually rather than a file downloaded. Bellevue turned out to be the easy version of that: one City page states a court count for every venue it lists, so the work was reading rather than reconstructing. Kirkland was the same shape and arrived by a different route - it had been refused outright on an HTTP 403 during an earlier run, and on retesting the site simply answered, which is a lesson about our own records rather than about Kirkland. Redmond is the pointed case here: it holds twelve imported records, more than any unpublished city in the county, and it still refuses our request with a 403 today. Kent, Renton, Auburn, Issaquah and Mercer Island are unread, and there is no reason to assume any of them publishes as well as Bellevue or Kirkland does. The threshold has not moved - three venues with a named source and a date - and the honest position remains that this page reports three cities out of twenty-eight in which we hold records.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in King County?
faqs.a: We do not know, and no honest page can tell you. What we can tell you is what we have checked: a hundred and forty-four courts across forty venues in three cities - ninety-two outdoor in Seattle, forty-two in Bellevue and ten in Kirkland - every one confirmed against a source we can show you. The county has thirty-nine cities and we have verified three.

faqs.q: Why are only three cities listed when King County has thirty-nine?
faqs.a: Because they are the only three whose courts we have been able to confirm against a named source. A city appears here once three or more of its venues carry a source and a date we can show you. Redmond, Kent, Auburn, Issaquah and Mercer Island all hold enough imported records to clear the threshold on volume, and not one of those records carries a source, so none of them is published. Redmond also still refuses our requests outright.

faqs.q: What made Seattle and Bellevue possible, and the rest of the county harder?
faqs.a: Two different kinds of luck. Seattle publishes a dedicated pickleball dataset through its GIS portal, listing court counts, lights, nets and restrooms per location, refreshed weekly — twenty-four venues from one authoritative file. Bellevue publishes no dataset at all, but it publishes one page that states a court count for every pickleball venue it runs, indoor and outdoor, and links each to a park page carrying the address. Neither is normal. Most cities publish a list of park names and leave you to guess.

faqs.q: Are the courts on this page free to use?
faqs.a: Not confirmed. Seattle Parks publishes locations, counts, lights and nets but no fee information, so every venue here shows cost as not verified rather than free. They are municipal park courts and are very likely free, but we do not print a likelihood as a fact. If you know otherwise and can point at a source, the help-us-verify link on any venue page reaches a real queue.

faqs.q: How often is this checked again?
faqs.a: The underlying Seattle dataset is refreshed weekly by the city and was last edited on 31 August 2026; we read it on 3 September 2026, and that date appears on every venue. We have not yet set a re-check cadence — how long a court count stays trustworthy before it needs looking at again is an open decision on this project, and until it is settled we show you the date and let you judge.

sources.evidence: Court counts and locations for every Seattle Parks pickleball site. Green Lake Park (East Courts), Bitter Lake Playfield and Rainier Beach Playfield each record 8 courts; Miller Playfield records 5.

sources.evidence: 151 imported rows carry a derived county of King, WA, across 28 distinct cities. 15 of those cities hold 3 or more rows. Seattle 53, Bellevue 12, Redmond 12, Kent 9, Auburn 7, Issaquah 6, Mercer Island 6, Renton 5. No row outside Seattle carries a qualifying source_url or a date_checked. This is a statement about the contents of our own import, not a census of King County.
